title: Twenty First Word First Station Fifth Warning Rejecting Worldly Busyness As An Excuse

questions.question: What problem is being talked about at the start of this passage?
questions.answer: Being lazy about worship and not doing the required prayers well.

questions.question: What two reasons are asked about for this laziness?
questions.answer: Being busy with worldly things and thinking there is not enough time because of work.

questions.question: According to the passage, were people made only to live for this world?
questions.answer: No. People were made for more than just this world.

questions.question: What example shows that a person is not meant to live only like an animal?
questions.answer: A person may be stronger in abilities, but even a small bird can do better at finding its daily food.

questions.question: What does that example teach about a human being’s main job?
questions.answer: A human being should work for an everlasting life, not only chase food and money.

questions.question: What mistake does the passage say many people make with worldly matters?
questions.answer: They get involved in small things that are not really important to them.

questions.question: What are two examples of useless things that waste time?
questions.answer: Spending time on faraway space facts and counting things in another country.

questions.question: Why is filling time with those kinds of facts called a waste?
questions.answer: Because it is like acting as if you will stay in the world for a very long time.

questions.question: In the story about wages, what is the worker offered for ten minutes of digging?
questions.answer: A very valuable reward.

questions.question: Why is it foolish for the worker to refuse in that story?
questions.answer: Because he gives up a huge gain to avoid a tiny loss.

questions.question: In the comparison, what does the orchard stand for?
questions.answer: A person’s work in this world to earn a living.

questions.question: What happens if a person leaves the required prayers while working?
questions.answer: The work only brings a small worldly gain.

questions.question: What good thing can a person do with break time?
questions.answer: Use it for prayer.

questions.question: What two big benefits are found through praying during those rest times?
questions.answer: Better blessing in worldly living and provision for the Hereafter.

questions.question: What loss comes from leaving the prayers?
questions.answer: A person misses great reward and loses strength and eagerness.

questions.question: What is the main warning in this passage about worship?
questions.answer: Do not let worldly busyness make you careless about prayer.

questions.question: When someone says, “I am too busy,” what two causes are mentioned?
questions.answer: Too many worldly jobs and trying to earn a living.

questions.question: What question helps the reader think about life’s purpose?
questions.answer: Whether a person was made only for this world.

questions.question: How does the passage compare a human and a sparrow?
questions.answer: A sparrow can do better at finding daily needs, even though a human has greater abilities in other ways.

questions.question: What should a person seek instead of living only for eating and earning?
questions.answer: A real life that lasts forever.

questions.question: What does the passage say about many things people call “important”?
questions.answer: Many of them are actually small and unnecessary.

questions.question: What is wrong with spending lots of time on trivia?
questions.answer: It pulls you away from what matters most.

questions.question: What feeling about life is hidden inside that mistake?
questions.answer: Living as if this world will last for you for a very long time.

questions.question: In the digging example, what is the small thing lost?
questions.answer: A little bit of daily pay.

questions.question: In that same example, what is the big thing that could be gained?
questions.answer: Something far more precious and valuable.

questions.question: What lesson should we learn from that comparison?
questions.answer: We should not leave a huge reward for the sake of a tiny worldly loss.

questions.question: In the orchard example, what does keeping up the required prayers protect?
questions.answer: The deeper value and reward of a person’s work.

questions.question: Why are rest times a good moment for prayer in this passage?
questions.answer: Because prayer gives calm to the soul and relief to the heart.

questions.question: What are the “two mines” meant to show?
questions.answer: Two great sources of benefit that come with work joined to prayer.

questions.question: What happens to someone who leaves prayer and misses these two mines?
questions.answer: He loses great wealth of reward and becomes weak in spirit.

questions.question: What does the passage ask the soul to think about first?
questions.answer: Whether being careless in prayer comes from being too busy with worldly life.

questions.question: Why is “I have no time” not a good excuse in this passage?
questions.answer: Because people often spend time on many things that are not truly necessary.

questions.question: What does the passage say a human is better at than animals?
questions.answer: Human abilities and higher qualities.

questions.question: What does it say a human is not better at than even a little bird?
questions.answer: Getting the simple needs of worldly life.

questions.question: What does that contrast help us understand?
questions.answer: A human being’s purpose is higher than only searching for food and money.

questions.question: What kind of life should a true human aim for?
questions.answer: A lasting life that continues forever.

questions.question: What is one sign that a person is too attached to worldly things?
questions.answer: He spends precious time learning details that do not really help him.

questions.question: Why are those details called “inessential”?
questions.answer: Because they are not the main things a person truly needs.

questions.question: In the example about work pay, what does the worker fear losing?
questions.answer: A small part of his daily earnings.

questions.question: What makes his excuse silly?
questions.answer: He refuses a much greater treasure for the sake of a tiny amount.

questions.question: How does that story connect to prayer?
questions.answer: Leaving prayer for worldly work is like missing a great treasure for a small gain.

questions.question: What does the orchard picture teach about earning a living?
questions.answer: Work for food is fine, but it should not push prayer away.

questions.question: If prayer is left out, how much benefit does work bring according to the passage?
questions.answer: Mostly only a low-level worldly living.

questions.question: If prayer is included, what happens to a person’s work time and break time?
questions.answer: The breaks become worship, and the work gains bigger value.

questions.question: What does prayer do for the spirit in this part of the passage?
questions.answer: It gives the spirit ease.

questions.question: What does prayer do for the heart here?
questions.answer: It lets the heart rest.

questions.question: What kind of soul is being warned in this part?
questions.answer: A soul that loves the world too much.

questions.question: What action shows this unhealthy love of the world?
questions.answer: Becoming lazy about worship and the required prayers.

questions.question: What question is used to challenge that way of thinking?
questions.answer: Whether a person was created only for worldly life.

questions.question: According to the passage, what can even a tiny bird do better than a human?
questions.answer: Find the basic things needed for daily living.

questions.question: If that is true, what does it say about the human mission?
questions.answer: It must be something higher than just getting food and worldly things.

questions.question: What kind of life should a human try to gain?
questions.answer: A true life that lasts forever.

questions.question: How does the passage describe many worldly jobs people chase?
questions.answer: They are often small matters people stick themselves into.

questions.question: What is a person forgetting when he fills his time with trivia?
questions.answer: The truly important duties.

questions.question: What attitude about time is criticized?
questions.answer: Acting as if one will live for hundreds and hundreds of years.

questions.question: In the example of the worker, what is offered for only a short effort?
questions.answer: A treasure worth much more than the lost pay.

questions.question: What does the short digging time stand for?
questions.answer: The small amount of time used for prayer.

questions.question: What does the tiny cut in pay stand for?
questions.answer: The little worldly loss a person fears when making time for prayer.

questions.question: What does the treasure stand for?
questions.answer: The great reward and benefit of worship.

questions.question: What would be the wise choice in that comparison?
questions.answer: To take the great treasure and not worry about the small loss.

questions.question: What does the passage call this world in the work example?
questions.answer: An orchard where a person labors for provision.

questions.question: If someone drops the required prayers, what remains from all that labor?
questions.answer: Only a narrow worldly living with little deeper benefit.

questions.question: If someone uses breaks for prayer, what two areas of life become richer?
questions.answer: Life in this world and life in the Hereafter.

questions.question: What kind of loss comes from leaving prayer, besides missing one act of worship?
questions.answer: Losing great hidden reward and inner strength.

questions.question: At the beginning, what is being blamed for weak worship?
questions.answer: Being overly busy with worldly concerns.

questions.question: What does the passage want the reader to ask about human life?
questions.answer: Whether human life is only for this world.

questions.question: What comparison is made with animals to teach this lesson?
questions.answer: Humans may be higher in ability, but not better at getting simple food than even a small bird.

questions.question: What does that comparison suggest about the goal of human life?
questions.answer: It should be much higher than just surviving.

questions.question: What kind of life is called the right one to strive for?
questions.answer: An everlasting life.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens when people focus too much on side matters?
questions.answer: They neglect what is truly important.

questions.question: Why are facts like faraway numbers and space details used as examples?
questions.answer: To show how people waste precious time on things that do not help their main duty.

questions.question: What wrong idea about life is hidden in that wasting of time?
questions.answer: Thinking there will always be plenty of time later.

questions.question: In the money example, what does the worker choose if he refuses to dig?
questions.answer: A tiny daily gain over a huge treasure.

questions.question: What feeling should that story create in the reader?
questions.answer: That refusing prayer for work is not sensible.

questions.question: What does the orchard symbolize in this passage?
questions.answer: A person’s place of work and effort in worldly life.

questions.question: What does abandoning prayer do to the fruits of that effort?
questions.answer: It limits them to only small worldly results.

questions.question: What special use of break time is encouraged?
questions.answer: Spending it in prayer.

questions.question: Why is prayer during breaks not called wasted time?
questions.answer: Because it refreshes the spirit and heart and brings more reward.

questions.question: What happens to morale when someone leaves the required prayers?
questions.answer: It becomes weak.

questions.question: What is the big topic of this passage?
questions.answer: Why we should not let worldly life pull us away from prayer.

questions.question: What two excuses for weak prayer are brought up first?
questions.answer: Being busy with worldly work and saying there is no time because of earning money.

questions.question: How does the passage answer the idea that worldly work is everything?
questions.answer: It says people were not made only for this world.

questions.question: What little creature is used to teach a lesson about getting daily food?
questions.answer: A sparrow.

questions.question: Why is that bird mentioned?
questions.answer: To show that human life must have a higher purpose than only finding food.

questions.question: What is that higher purpose described as?
questions.answer: Seeking a real life that lasts forever.

questions.question: What does the passage say about many “worldly occupations”?
questions.answer: Many are small matters people should not spend so much time on.

questions.question: What are the examples about space and counting used to show?
questions.answer: People can waste precious time on things that are not truly important.

questions.question: What false idea is a person living by when he does that?
questions.answer: That he has a very long life ahead in this world.

questions.question: In the example of the worker and the treasure, what is the main lesson?
questions.answer: Do not give up a huge gain to protect a tiny worldly amount.

questions.question: How is prayer like the short digging time in that story?
questions.answer: It takes a little time but brings great reward.

questions.question: How is lost pay like worldly worry?
questions.answer: It is a small thing people fear too much.

questions.question: What does the orchard stand for in the next example?
questions.answer: The place where a person works for daily provision.

questions.question: If prayer is dropped, what kind of result is left from that work?
questions.answer: Only a small worldly outcome.

questions.question: If prayer is kept, what happens to the value of a person’s life and work?
questions.answer: It gains much more benefit for this life and the next.

questions.question: What two parts of a person are especially helped by prayer during rest time?
questions.answer: The spirit and the heart.

questions.question: What is lost when a person leaves prayer?
questions.answer: Great reward, strong morale, and eagerness for good work.

questions.question: What may happen to that person’s attitude in old age?
questions.answer: He may become tired, uninterested, and lazy.

questions.question: What different attitude belongs to the person who prays?
questions.answer: He wants to keep increasing worship and good lawful effort.

questions.question: Why does he want to do that?
questions.answer: To prepare for the grave and the Hereafter.

questions.question: What does the short summary teach about time?
questions.answer: The past is gone and the future is not promised.

questions.question: So what time should a smart person use well?
questions.answer: The present day.
